measure.method:
Raw-CDP harness at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-thingsboard095-tb-thingsboard-io/3973666f-bba9-429b-a45b-e0ddba54c47a/scratchpad/inp/run.mjs, run against PRODUCTION https://thingsboard.io/pricing/ on Oct 12 2026. Setup: headless Chrome 155.0.8059.39, Node 22 global WebSocket, no repo files touched. Each run gets a fresh --user-data-dir (cold cache). The default consent state was kept: the banner was shown, nothing was clicked on it, and at the end of every run the banner was still visible with no tb_consent cookie and no googletagmanager request.

GPU: headless Chrome's default here is SwiftShader, meaning software raster and software compositing (confirmed with SystemInfo.getInfo). That inflated presentation delay heavily: a no-op click took 40 ms and calculator interactions with the backdrop-filter modal open took 120-200 ms. All headline numbers therefore use --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist --use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl on the AMD Radeon (Renoir) iGPU. The software-GL run is kept for comparison only (out-desktop-1x.json).

Instrumentation, injected before any page script (Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument): PerformanceObserver 'event' (durationThreshold 16, buffered), 'first-input', and 'long-animation-frame' (buffered). LoAF entries keep scripts[] (sourceURL, sourceFunctionName, invoker, invokerType, duration, forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration, sourceCharPosition) plus renderStart and styleAndLayoutStart, all on window.__inp.

Profiles:
- mobile-4x: 412x823, dpr 1.75, mobile:true, touch emulation, Android UA, CPU 4x.
- desktop-1x: 1350x940, no throttle.
- desktop-4x: 1350x940, CPU 4x.
- Worst profile (mobile-4x) repeated with Network.setBlockedURLs for 3P hosts.

Input is always trusted CDP input:
- Desktop: Input.dispatchMouseEvent (mouseMoved, wait 120 ms, mousePressed, 70 ms, mouseReleased).
- Mobile: Input.dispatchTouchEvent (touchStart, 70 ms, touchEnd). Coordinates are corrected by visualViewport.offsetLeft/offsetTop: the first mobile pass had a mapping bug and its files are archived as *-coordbug.json and not used.
- Keys: Input.dispatchKeyEvent for ArrowRight and digits; the element is focused through JS so the focus itself is not counted as an interaction.

Per interaction: scrollIntoView(center, instant), wait 300 ms plus 2 rAF, then an elementFromPoint check before acting. The harness refuses the action if the hit lands on a[href], the chat launcher, an iframe or the consent banner. Then it acts and settles 900 ms (1x) or 1500 ms (4x).

Matching and attribution:
- Event Timing entries are grouped by interactionId and duration = max entry.
- The split groups same-frame entries of the worst phase (e.g. pointerup and click): delay = processingStart - startTime; processing = sum of handler time; presentation = remainder. rAF-phase script counts as presentation.
- Overlapping LoAFs give script attribution and forced style/layout.
- Performance.getMetrics deltas are recorded for each interaction.
- Every interaction runs 3 reps; sub-tabs run full cycles and toggles alternate state.

Idle: 5 s after load + 5 s idle, using a trace (devtools.timeline, frame, toplevel, blink, cc) plus Performance.getMetrics, giving frames/s, recalc and layout counts and ms/s, and per-thread busy ms/s.

Ablations (same harness):
- --noanim: animation:none on html and #chat-launcher.
- --nosmil: SVGSVGElement.pauseAnimations().
- --reducedmotion: Emulation prefers-reduced-motion:reduce, the production code path that hides .pricing-bg-svg and stops chat-hues.
- --dropscriptrule / --droprule: delete one CSS rule via CSSOM.
- --block3p.
- --dpr=2.
- '--quick' runs are 1-rep subsets.

Root-cause tracing used itrace.mjs (one traced click, with optional invalidationTracking) and idletrace.mjs (with SelectorStats). Bisecting the :has() rules was done by deleting rule subsets via CSSOM.

measure.worst_interactions:
How to read the numbers: each run has about 105 measured interactions. INP-est is the 98th-percentile rule, i.e. the worst interaction after skipping one per 50. Durations are Event Timing values, rounded to 8 ms. Every split below is input delay / processing / presentation.

DESKTOP-1x (GPU on): median 48, p75 48, INP-est 56, max 64.
1. PAYG slider ArrowRight: 56 / 56 / 64 ms (split 0 / 16 / 48).
2. PC calc slider click: 56 ms (split 0 / 0 / 56).
3. PC slider ArrowRight: 56 ms (split 1 / 0 / 55).
- No LoAF over 50 ms on any of them. Presentation dominates.
- Even a no-op background click costs 40 ms (split 2 / 0 / 38). A trivial calibration page in the same browser gives under 16 ms.
- The cause is frame-pipeline latency from the page's never-ending animations, so every frame has to be re-rasterised. The GPU process main thread was busy about 654 ms/s at idle in the trace.
- With CSS animations off and the SVG waves (SMIL) paused, the median falls to 24 and the no-op click to under 16. At dpr 2 the numbers were the same.

DESKTOP-4x: median 72, p75 112, INP-est 176, max 184.
1. PAYG slider ArrowRight: 176 / 184 / 184 ms (split 1 / 63 / 120).
   - INPUT#sm-slider.onchange runs calculate(): 63 ms, of which 58 is forced style/layout.
   - The rAF calculate() adds 51 ms (44 forced).
2. PC calc slider click: 160 ms (split 1 / 0 / 159).
   - The rAF callback calc-tb-pc:15948 runs calculate(): 86 ms (78 forced). Because it runs in rAF, it shows up as presentation.
3. PC add-on switch: 160 / 152 / 160 ms (split 2 / 92 / 66).
   - INPUT#pc-edge-toggle.onchange: 91 ms (83 forced).
- Next worst:
  - Calculator open: 120-152 ms. BUTTON.onclick 75-80 ms, 66-71 forced, from lockScroll/open.
  - Sub-tab Cloud→Private Cloud: 104-112 ms (split 1 / 43 / 68). DIV.onclick activateSubTab spends 42 ms with 38 forced: the void el.offsetWidth reflow after the display swap restyles 864 elements and lays out 1243 objects.
  - Region and billing toggles: 64-88 ms. No script; inside mouseup default handling the browser restyles 1144 elements and lays out 1039 objects for the ~550-element region block swap.
  - Theme toggle: 80-88 ms (full restyle).

MOBILE-4x (touch): median 104, p75 136, INP-est 200, max 216. Zero interactions under 16 ms.
1. PAYG slider ArrowRight: 216 ms (split 0 / 78 / 138). This is a keyboard interaction, so it is less representative on phones.
2. PAYG Edge add-on switch tap: 216 ms (split 13 / 60 / 143).
   - The #sm-devices onblur handler runs calculate(): 61 ms. This is the previous input's blur, billed to this tap.
   - The toggle onchange handler runs calculate(): 59 ms.
   - Together they force 108 ms of style/layout.
3. PC add-on switch tap: 200 ms (split 46 / 84 / 70). onchange 83 ms (77 forced).
- Next worst:
  - PC calculator open: 192 ms (split 47 / 80 / 65).
  - Sub-tab Cloud→Private Cloud: 168 ms (split 52 / 37 / 79).
- Mobile-specific: every tap carries 30-77 ms of input delay, even the no-op tap (64 ms = 37 / 1 / 26). The cause is idle main-thread load: the renderer main thread is about 600 ms/s busy (see idle_activity).

MOBILE-4x with third parties blocked: median 104, INP-est 192, max 224. Same as unblocked.
1. PC stepper +: 224 ms (split 128 / 39 / 57). The input delay is the onblur calculate() left over from the preceding typing.
2. PAYG Edge add-on switch: 224 ms (split 123 / 53 / 48).
3. Sub-tab Cloud→Private Cloud: 192 ms (split 56 / 46 / 90).

ROOT CAUSES, each confirmed by ablation:
(a) One Starlight markdown.css rule, shipped inline on /pricing/ although no .sl-markdown-content exists on the page:
    .sl-markdown-content :is(ol,ul):has(…) > li > :is(…, :not(script):has(~ script:last-child):not(:has(~ :not(script))))
   - Invalidation tracing shows "Invalidation set invalidates subtree… allDescendantsMightBeInvalid" on html and div.page for every DOM insertion.
   - So each calculator calculate() (innerHTML) restyles all 1114 rendered elements 2-3 times, about 20-35 ms each at 4x.
   - Bisection: deleting that single rule drops the calculator restyle to 130 elements. Deleting all 94 :has() rules gives 77.
   - Effect at desktop-4x: calculator interactions fall from 112-184 to 64-88 ms (PAYG ArrowRight 184→80, PC slider 160→80) and the max over labels from 184 to 96.
   - The rule is in node_modules/@astrojs/starlight/dist/style/markdown.css. The files in the local pnpm store show it in Starlight 0.37.1 through 0.42.4, so it has been live since the Astro launch.
(b) Never-ending animations:
   - Four SMIL <animateTransform> waves in src/components/Pricing/PricingBackground.astro, present since the page was created in March. They cause a style recalc, a layout and a full-layer GPU re-raster every frame. getAnimations() does not report them, and PSI's "non-composited animations" audit misses them.
   - #chat-launcher chat-hues, a 15 s infinite animation added Oct 6 (#720).
   - The promo-collapse scroll-timeline on :root.
   - Stopping all of them: mobile-4x median 104→64, INP-est 200→160, tap input delay ~40-75 → 6-19 ms, no-op tap 64 → under 16.
   - The production prefers-reduced-motion path gives the same mobile median of 64.
(c) Mobile only (<432px wide, consent banner shown): the rule `:root:has(#cc-main .cm:not([hidden])) .chat-launcher` (src/components/YourGptWidget.astro:120) is re-matched on every chat-hues frame.
   - SelectorStats puts it at about 3.7 ms of each 7.4 ms recalc.
   - Deleting only this rule cuts idle recalc from 575 to 104 ms/s.
   - Interactions improve only modestly: median 104→100, light taps 8-30 ms faster.
(d) Forced synchronous reflows in page and calculator scripts:
   - activateSubTab: void el.offsetWidth.
   - calculate(): reads scrollTop between innerHTML writes.
   - lockScroll when a calculator opens.
   - A blur-triggered calculate() charges the next tap.

Combined fix, mobile-4x (rule deleted + reduced motion): per-label median 104→48, max 216→120.
Combined fix, desktop-4x (rule deleted only): per-label median 80→64, max 184→96.
measure.caveats:
1. Lab vs field. A Ryzen (Cezanne) CPU throttled 4x is not a real phone. CDP CPU throttling slows only the renderer, not the GPU process or raster threads. The per-frame SMIL re-raster cost (GPU main thread ~490-650 ms/s in the lab) will be much worse on weak phone GPUs, so GPU-bound presentation delay is probably underestimated.

2. Headless GPU mode changes everything. Default headless uses SwiftShader software raster and compositing. In that mode the desktop-1x numbers were median 72, INP-est 192, max 200 (calculator interactions with the backdrop-filter modal at 120-200 ms, mostly presentation). With the real GPU they were median 48, INP-est 56. All headline numbers use the GPU-enabled runs.

3. Measurement limits:
   - Event Timing reports nothing under 16 ms and rounds to 8 ms. A 0 in the tables means under 16 ms.
   - LoAF lists only scripts over 5 ms. Long frames with no script attributed (region and billing toggles) were explained with a separate trace.
   - "presentation" includes rAF-phase script, because the calculator's scheduleCalculate() runs calculate() inside rAF.
   - The quick ablation runs ('--quick') are 1 rep each.

4. INP-est comes from about 105 scripted interactions in one session. Field INP is a per-visit worst case taken at p75 across visits, and real visits have far fewer interactions. Treat the per-interaction numbers as the result, not the INP-est.

5. Consent state was left at default: banner visible, no tb_consent cookie, verified at the end of every run.
   - GTM (GTM-TGBNQXN) never loads without consent, so its cost for consented visitors is unmeasured.
   - YourGPT loads only when the launcher is clicked, which was never done.
   - The visible banner is exactly what activates the expensive mobile :root:has(#cc-main…) rule. Visitors who already made a choice do not pay that particular cost.

6. Timing and history:
   - Prod HTML is the Oct 12 build. chat-hues and its :has rule shipped on Oct 6 (#720), so they are not behind the Jun–Aug CrUX rise; they will appear in coming CrUX windows.
   - Until Oct 6 the YourGPT script was injected on idle about 10 s after load for every visitor (commit 58e9b28a0). That is a field cost these lab runs do not reproduce.
   - The SMIL waves and the Starlight rule have been live since the May launch.
   - I did not measure historical builds, so the Jun–Aug step remains unexplained here. The promo banner and its scroll-timeline (#449, #505 in June) are only candidates.

7. Harness details:
   - Keyboard interactions on mobile (ArrowRight) are less realistic for touch users.
   - The press length is synthetic (70 ms).
   - The region defaulted to EU from this machine's location.
   - Hover (tooltips, desktop mega-menu) is not an INP interaction and measured under 16 ms.
   - The comparison table has no expand toggles, so none were measured.
   - The first mobile pass had a touch-coordinate bug (visual-viewport offset). Three taps landed on non-interactive elements: the consent-banner description text and plan-card headings, never a control. Those files are archived as *-coordbug.json and excluded.

8. Side finding, not verified on a real device: with the Private Cloud tab active on 412px, documentElement.scrollWidth is 485 (body 412), which widens the layout viewport. Candidates are the fixed .sub-tab-tooltip elements parked off-screen right (right up to 570px) and the 500px .pc-comparison-table.

9. The only third-party request seen was api.github.com, so blocking third parties changed nothing measurable (differences within ±16 ms noise).

measure.idle_activity:
Idle = 5 s after load + 5 s quiet, default state, measured with a trace plus Performance.getMetrics.

Desktop-1x:
- Continuous 60 frames/s (300 BeginMainThreadFrame in 5 s).
- 75 style recalcs/s (36 ms/s; 18 elements each: 14 = chat-launcher, 4 = SMIL <g>).
- 75 layouts/s (5 ms/s); the per-frame layout comes from the SMIL transform attribute.
- Renderer task 113 ms/s.
- GPU-process main thread about 654 ms/s in the desktop-1x trace: continuous re-raster of the masked, 3D-rotated background SVG layer.

Desktop-4x:
- 60 frames/s; recalc 112 ms/s, layout 17 ms/s, renderer task 369 ms/s.
- Thread busy: renderer main 273 ms/s, GPU main 635 ms/s.
- Each frame also does a synthetic mousemove hit test of 2-3 ms when the cursor is over the page.

Mobile-4x:
- 60 frames/s, but style recalc costs 575 ms/s (77 recalcs/s at about 7 ms each, still only 18 elements).
- Renderer task 809 ms/s; thread busy renderer main 602 ms/s, GPU main 486 ms/s.
- So the main thread is about 60-80% busy while the page sits idle. That explains the 30-77 ms input delay on every tap.
- Cause of the mobile style cost: `@media (width<432px) :root:has(#cc-main .cm:not([hidden])) .chat-launcher` is re-matched every chat-hues frame. SelectorStats: 1.89 s of selector time over 516 recalcs, versus about 0.13 ms per recalc in total on desktop.

Ablations:

Mobile-4x, only that rule deleted:
- Recalc 104 ms/s, renderer 252 ms/s, GPU 490 ms/s.
- Interactions: median 104→100, light taps 8-30 ms faster.

CSS animations off, SMIL still running:
- Desktop-1x: recalc 7 ms/s, but 60 frames/s and layouts continue, and the floor stays 40-48 ms.
- Desktop-4x: renderer 230 ms/s, GPU 701 ms/s.
- Mobile-4x: renderer 170 ms/s, GPU 479 ms/s.

Everything off (CSS animation:none on html/#chat-launcher + SMIL paused):
- 0 frames, ~0 ms/s on all threads.

Effect of stopping all animations on interactions:
- Desktop-1x: median 48→24, no-op click 40→under 16, max 64→48.
- Desktop-4x: light interactions (no-op, accordion, FAQ, header) 32-40 → 16-24 ms; heavy script/layout interactions unchanged; per-label median 80→64.
- Mobile-4x (3 reps): median 104→64, p75 136→88, INP-est 200→160, max 216→176. Tap input delay drops from 30-77 to 6-19 ms; no-op tap 64→under 16; FAQ tab 88→32; burger 88→32.

prefers-reduced-motion (production path: hides .pricing-bg-svg, no chat-hues):
- Idle 0 frames.
- Mobile-4x median 64, max 168.
- Plus deleting the Starlight :has rule: median 48, max 120.
measure.third_party_effect:
Third parties make no measurable difference in the default consent state.

Method. Read every file in the area. Fetched the prod HTML (825KB) and counted elements with a parser. Profiled on live prod in the Browser pane (Chrome 152, 1024x768, DPR 1, fast desktop; cookie consent untouched, so GTM was not loaded). The pane was hidden, so no frames were produced: paint and raster could not be measured, and the numbers below are synchronous main-thread costs (handler plus forced style and layout). The page was reloaded afterwards to undo test mutations.

DOM size:
- 5,995 live elements; .pricing-page holds 5,064.
- FAQ: 2,886 elements in 3 blocks (cloud 973 / pc 916 / pe 996; 245 items), all in the DOM and toggled with display.
- Sections: Cloud 1,101 (NA 547 / EU 543, each with 5 plans, 30 features, 14 info icons, 3 add-ons, 11 top-ups); Private Cloud 606 (4 plans, 20 features, 14-row table); On-premises 425 (payg 284 with 4 plans and 24 features / perpetual 118).
- Calculator modals sit outside the page root (~500 nodes).
- Before Sep 29 the page carried 506 FAQ items in 8 contexts plus TBMQ and CE sections, so the DOM was roughly 1.6-1.8x today's.
- The CrUX window ending Oct 9 holds only ~11 days of the slimmer 4.4 page. Re-check field INP around Oct 27 before attributing anything to the current DOM.

Measured per-interaction costs on desktop, before paint:
- Sub-tab switch: 7-11ms. Forced offsetWidth layout is 4.3-8.2ms of that.
- Region switch: ~6-9ms.
- On-premises billing switch: 5.5-9ms, max 17.
- Private Cloud billing switch: 4.6-6.6ms.
- Phones are likely 4-6x slower: about 25-65ms each, plus raster.
- Trusted clicks produced no Event Timing entry of 16ms or more on this machine.
- So on desktop, this area's handlers alone do not explain a p75 of 166ms. The main drivers for desktop are probably outside it: GTM for consented users, calculators, FAQ, chat and promo. One more candidate is the target=_blank CTA hypothesis below.

Biggest finding (site-wide, but it inflates this area): any child-list mutation costs a near-whole-document style recalc. That covers textContent=, replaceChildren, and inserting or removing an element anywhere on the page.
- textContent=: 6-13ms of style. Changing Text.data costs ~0.
- Inserting or removing an element: ~8-11ms style + 5-12ms layout.
- Cause, confirmed by deleting rules through CSSOM on prod:
  - Removing the 34 Starlight `.sl-markdown-content ...:has()` rules took structural-mutation style cost from 6.1ms to 1.6ms. This page has no .sl-markdown-content element, so those rules are pure overhead from inlining the whole site's CSS.
  - Removing the 31 `header.header:has(...)` rules brought it to 0.5ms.
  - Removing all 94 brought it to 0.
- In this area it hits On-premises billing (heading and subtitle textContent) and Private Cloud billing (4 price textContent writes). It also hits every DOM-building interaction elsewhere: calculator results, FAQ, cookie banner, YourGPT injection.
- Fix direction: stop inlining docs and Starlight CSS into marketing pages, or scope those :has rules. Locally, update Text.data instead of textContent.

Other concrete fixes in this area:
1. activateSubTab: return early when sectionId === activeSubTab. Drop `void el.offsetWidth`; use @starting-style, a double-rAF, or element.animate for the fade.
2. Yield before non-visual work. Do the DOM swap first, then run reportPriceOpen, updateFaqVisibility, updateUrl and the GTM push after paint (rAF + setTimeout or scheduler.yield).
3. Put content-visibility:auto with contain-intrinsic-size on FAQ blocks and inactive regions, or render FAQ answers lazily, so show/hide of ~1,000-node blocks is cheaper.
4. Replace the SMIL background with a static image, or a pre-rendered layer animated with a composited CSS transform. Alternatively drop the mask, or pause the animation after a few seconds or while the user interacts.
5. continuous_work.what: Full-viewport .calc-modal-overlay with backdrop-filter: blur(4px), plus 300ms open/close transitions of opacity, background (main-thread paint), backdrop-filter and wrapper transform
continuous_work.why_it_matters: While a calculator is open, every frame that has to be produced re-composites a blurred full-viewport backdrop. Frames are produced by every in-modal interaction and by the page's own infinite animations under it (promo-collapse on <html>, chat-hues on #chat-launcher). In headless Chrome on prod, the frame rate dropped from 60fps (16.7ms) to 15fps (66.7ms) as soon as the modal opened, with no scripts and under 1ms of style/layout. Injecting backdrop-filter:none restored 16.7ms frames; pausing all CSS animations alone did not. Headless uses software compositing, so the absolute cost is inflated: real desktop GPUs handle this easily, and low-end Android GPUs pay less than headless but still pay. It lands in the presentation delay of every in-modal interaction, which is why the desktop headless INP for toggles and steppers was 150-230ms while processing was only 12-23ms.

maps.notes:
The biggest finding is cross-cutting rather than calculator-specific: one rule in Starlight's CSS makes small DOM changes restyle the whole rendered page. I confirmed it on prod. The rule is `.sl-markdown-content :is(ol, ul):has(> li > :not(a, strong, ...)) > li > :is(... :has(~ script:last-child):not(:has(~ :not(script))))`, in node_modules/@astrojs/starlight/dist/style/markdown.css:46-58 (layer starlight.content). It ships in the pricing page's 230 KB of inline CSS even though the page has no .sl-markdown-content element.
- **What the trace shows:** Chrome logs "Invalidation set invalidates subtree, allDescendantsMightBeInvalid" naming this selector. Every forced style recalc caused by a small DOM mutation then restyles about 1,700-1,800 elements (the whole rendered page) instead of the roughly 100-250 the calculator actually changed.
- **How I isolated it:** I deleted rules one at a time through CSSOM. Deleting the print `:has(~footer)` and `nth-last-child(1 of ...)` rules changed nothing. Deleting only this Starlight rule cut a PC calculate() from 16.9ms to 7.8ms on desktop and from 72.8ms to 31.8ms on mobile with 4x CPU throttle (time to next frame 112 -> 48ms). Recalc counts fell from 1,718-1,785 to 66-243.
- **It is not limited to the calculators:** sub-tab switch on mobile 4x went from 30.1 to 21.8ms synchronous (64 -> 55ms to next frame), and the region toggle from 48.7 to 40.3ms to next frame. This is likely site-wide; pricing feels it more because of its large DOM (6,000 elements) and many mutating interactions.
- **When it shipped:** it went live with the 2026-06-30 main merge (Starlight 0.38.4 -> 0.39.2), which matches the mid-July to August INP rise.
- **Possible fixes (for the owner):** don't ship Starlight markdown.css on non-doc layouts, `pnpm patch` the selector, or raise it upstream with Starlight.

**How I measured:** headless Chrome 149 against prod https://thingsboard.io/pricing/. Consent was rejected, so GTM was not loaded. Inputs were real (Playwright mouse/keyboard, recorded through Event Timing + LoAF), plus traces with invalidation tracking. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-thingsboard095-tb-thingsboard-io/3973666f-bba9-429b-a45b-e0ddba54c47a/scratchpad/ (inp-calc.mjs, trace.mjs, inval.mjs, rules.mjs, ab.mjs, diag.mjs, snap.mjs, counts.mjs); I edited no repository files.

**Calculator numbers:**
| Interaction | Desktop (unthrottled) | Mobile, 4x CPU throttle |
|---|---|---|
| Toggles, steppers, sliders, mode/profile/billing | processing 12-23ms, 70-90% forced style/layout | INP 120-216ms, processing 60-113ms |
| Modal re-open | INP 48-72ms (processing 14-23ms) | INP 128ms (processing 76ms) |
| First open (click itself) | INP 40-56ms | INP 48-88ms |
| First open (init task after the chunk arrives) | not measured | LoAF 170-257ms |

Headless presentation delay is inflated by the backdrop-filter compositing (see continuous_work), so the in-modal desktop INP of 120-232ms overstates real desktops.

**Answers to the specific questions:**
- **Does the range slider re-render on every tick?** Input events are rAF-coalesced (one render per frame, still inside the presented frame). The PAYG `change` handler also renders synchronously, so every PAYG click or arrow-key press renders twice (calc-tb-payg.ts:323-324).
- **How much DOM does each recompute rewrite?** PAYG: results 63-122 elements + footer 12. PC: results 103-249 elements + total row about 11, and an added profile is about 100 elements. Each recompute also does 2 (PAYG) or 2-3 (PC) forced style+layout passes, from the `scrollTop` read/write around `results.innerHTML` (payg:239/303, pc:624/675). Each pass restyles about 1,800 elements because of the Starlight rule.
- **What about the JS itself?** Number formatting with toLocaleString and string building is only about 10% of the cost.

**How much this explains of field INP:** calculator handlers can't by themselves explain the 166ms (desktop) / 319ms (phone) p75 for /pricing/. They are reachable only from 'Estimate your cost' on the Private Cloud and On-premises tabs (Cloud is the default) and from 3 FAQ links. On desktop, main-thread cost is well under 100ms. They do produce phone INPs of roughly 150-250ms for the sessions that use them. What does reach the page-level INP is the Starlight `:has()` tax described above, which applies to every interaction.

**Out of INP scope, but should be fixed:**
- **PAYG slider bug:** the `change` guard `if (v <= 4)` (calc-tb-payg.ts:324) is always true since the Sep 29 change to max=3. Releasing the slider anywhere in the 1,000-150,000 range snaps to 1,000 or 150,000. Verified on prod: dragged to 57,620, released, got 1,000.
- **Dead code:** CalculatorInline.astro has had no importers since Sep 29.
- **Calculator path, cheaper with the rule fixed or not:** remove the scrollTop save/restore (or read it before any writes), stop running calculate() a second time on PAYG change, and consider dropping the full-viewport backdrop-filter.

maps.notes:
BOTTOM LINE FOR MY AREA. The below-the-fold components are not what drives the pricing INP regression. Their DOM work is small. The interaction costs that matter are:
(a) Synchronous analytics pushes inside handlers. A FAQ open makes 1 push; an (i)-icon jump makes 2 (PriceOpen + faq_node_interaction). With GTM loaded (everyone until Oct 7), each push runs GTM trigger evaluation and the GA4 tag in the input task.
(b) The (i)-icon → FAQ jump path. It needlessly re-runs activateSubTab on the already-active tab: a forced reflow at index.astro:682, an opacity-transition restart on the ~550-element section, a spurious PriceOpen event and replaceState.
(c) The FAQ context swap inside every sub-tab switch, about 25–35% of that interaction's rendering work.

MEASURED ON PROD. Browser pane, 1024×768, desktop CPU unthrottled, no consent given so GTM was not loaded. Each figure is processing plus forced style and layout:
- FAQ toggle: 0.1 ms
- Category switch: 1.5–1.9 ms
- Load more (11 items): 2.6 ms
- (i) add-on jump: 2.9 ms (Event Timing processing 2 ms)
- Top-up toggle: about 0 ms
- FAQ block swap: 1.8–3.3 ms
- Sub-tab switch, for reference: 6–10 ms
- Full-document :root custom-property recalc: 4–6 ms
Phones are roughly 4–6× slower.

Caveats:
- Event Timing presentation delays came back as 10–16 s and are artifacts: the shared browser pane was hidden and frame production was throttled. Only the processing numbers are valid.
- Another agent was using the same pane (a 390×844 emulation appeared mid-run, and a cruxvis tab is open). I stopped using the browser and did not reset their viewport.
- GTM push cost is an estimate. Measuring it would need consent and would send live GA hits, which I did not do.

DOM SIZE.
Prod HTML is 825 KB uncompressed and parses to 5,995 elements, with a maximum depth of 21. Of these, about 815 have a box at default state (Cloud, EU; live checkVisibility). A static estimate per tab gives about 1,160 for Cloud, 1,233 for Private Cloud and 910 for On-premises. Inline <style> is 229 KB; the CSSOM is about 269 KB with 1,272 rules.

Breakdown:
- FAQ: 2,885 elements, 48% of the DOM. 3 contexts × 22 categories (8/6/8) × 245 items (88/70/87). 6 items show per category before Load more. Only 1 context × 1 category is rendered at a time, about 60–110 elements. Collapsed answers in that category are fully laid out (grid 0fr plus overflow:hidden), not skipped.
- Plan-card grids: about 1,064 (Cloud NA 308, Cloud EU 304, Private Cloud 229, On-premises PAYG 223). Only one set is rendered.
- AddOnsSection: 5 instances × 53–58 elements, 15 FAQ-jump triggers.
- TopUpsSection: 2 instances × 177 elements (22 items each, 44 headers).
- ComparisonTable: the only DataTable on the page. 13 rows × (1 th + 4 td) = 65 cells, about 150 elements, 9 triggers. Rendered only on the Private Cloud tab. It has no expand/collapse and no sticky header; the only sticky element in my area is the FAQ category sidebar.
- Perpetual block: about 117. Calculator modals: about 250 (display:none). Header: about 450. Footer: 78.
- Positioned tooltips: 76 in total, 20 rendered (fixed, visibility:hidden).

History: the Jekyll page in March 2026 (Wayback) had 4,205 elements. From the mid-May launch to Sep 29 the page also rendered CE and TBMQ: 8 FAQ contexts (~506 items) and 16 pricing-section blocks. Before Jul 2, each FAQ row also carried 2 inline SVGs. I estimate roughly 10–14k elements in that period; this is from the data, not a build.

KEY EXPERIMENT. Detaching all 4,637 display:none elements (5,995 → 1,358) left a full-document style recalc unchanged: 4.7 ms before, 4.6 ms after. Blink does not style display:none subtrees, so hidden-but-rendered DOM is not an INP factor here; the 4.4 DOM halving should not be expected to move INP. What every full recalc pays is the rendered DOM (about 0.8–1.2k) times the large global CSSOM. The querySelectorAll walks over the whole document (scroll listener, paas links) cost about 0.005 ms.

RECOMMENDATIONS. Not applied; this was a read-only task.
1. In scrollToFaqItem (index.astro:711-721), skip activateSubTab when the owning tab is already active. This removes the forced reflow, the section opacity restart and layer promotion, replaceState, and a spurious PriceOpen event, which also inflates PriceOpen analytics.
2. Move trackFaq and reportPriceOpen pushes out of the input task, for example `await scheduler.yield?.()` or `requestAnimationFrame(() => setTimeout(push, 0))`, so GTM processing runs after the next paint. The same pattern applies to every dataLayer/gtag call in pricing handlers.
3. Add `content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto <h>` to .pricing-faq, .topups-section, .addons-section, .pc-comparison-section (and the footer). This lets every full-document style and layout pass skip off-screen below-the-fold subtrees: the per-frame :root --promo-cur recalc, tab switches, theme changes.
4. Optional: skip layout of collapsed FAQ answers, for example with content-visibility:hidden on a collapsed .faq-answer-overflow, or details/::details-content. Low priority.
5. Do not spend effort lazy-rendering inactive FAQ contexts for INP. Measurement shows no style-recalc benefit; only HTML bytes and parse time would improve.

CROSS-CUTTING (outside my area, for the synthesizer):
- The GTM container GTM-TGBNQXN is 529 KB. It registers gtm.click (23 click-trigger entries), linkClick, scrollDepth (2 listeners, 25/50/75/90%) and a 3 s timer, and uses _css "matches selector" predicates. These run on every click and scroll on the long pricing page whenever GTM is loaded.
- PriceOpen is pushed via gtag on every tab activation, including the init and the (i) re-activation.
- Sub-tab switching (6–10 ms on desktop, including the forced reflow at :682) is the heaviest page-specific interaction I measured. Even ×5 on a phone it does not reach 300 ms, which points the phone p75 at third-party and main-thread contention (GTM, YourGPT, continuous animations) rather than page DOM work.

Now: the first #chat-launcher click (whenChatLoaded). Once loaded it reacts to every DOM childList mutation and every URL change.

Inside its component `lpt()`: a setInterval every 1s calls setState and writes sessionStorage('timeSpent'), so the component re-renders every second. A burst of 200 childList mutations cost 0.6 ms without the widget, then 1.2 ms after 15s, 2.3 ms after 45s and 3.3 ms after 89s on the page, growing linearly with dwell time.

candidates.title: A Starlight 0.39 list rule shipped onto /pricing/ on Jun 30 makes every DOM insertion or removal restyle the whole page
candidates.mechanism: Phases: processing for forced style inside handlers, and presentation for the rAF calculate(). The rule is `.sl-markdown-content :is(ol, ul):has(> li > :not(a, strong, …, ol, ul)) > li > :is(…)`. Because the :has() is not in the subject position, Blink invalidates the whole document subtree on ANY child-list mutation (innerHTML, textContent=, appendChild/remove). Each forced or frame style pass then restyles every rendered element (~1,100-1,800) instead of the ~100-250 that changed. Pricing interactions hit by this: every calculator calculate() (results.innerHTML plus a scrollTop read and write, so 2-3 forced passes, and 2 calculate() calls per PAYG slider change), calculator open (lockScroll), On-prem billing (heading and subtitle textContent), PC billing (4 price textContent writes). The rule never matches on /pricing/ because the page has no .sl-markdown-content. It is there only because src/components/starlight/MarkdownContent.astro statically imports DocMarkdownContent.astro, which imports markdown.css. Astro bundles CSS by import graph, so every BaseLayout (StarlightPage) route inlines it, even though the comment in MarkdownContent.astro says the split keeps it out. Correction to the measure area: it named this the `:has(~ script:last-child)` rule. My CSSOM bisection on prod shows that clause, present since Starlight 0.37, costs nothing. candidates.title: Never-ending SMIL wave background keeps the main thread and GPU busy every frame (pricing-only)
candidates.mechanism: Phases: presentation delay on every interaction, plus input delay on phones. PricingBackground has 4 `<animateTransform repeatCount=indefinite>` on full-height wave paths inside a position:fixed SVG with `transform: rotate(-28deg) rotateY(-6deg)`, perspective 1400px and a CSS mask-image. The box is about 3.4x the viewport area on desktop and 220%x110% on mobile. SMIL is not composited, so on every vsync, forever, the renderer runs SMIL tick, SVG style and layout, and paint. The GPU process then re-rasters the whole masked layer: about 654 ms/s busy at idle on desktop-1x and about 486 ms/s on mobile-4x. Each interaction's frame queues behind that pipeline. This is invisible to Lighthouse, because its non-composited-animations audit and getAnimations() do not report SMIL. Only prefers-reduced-motion disables it. No other page has it, which fits /pricing/ desktop INP being about 2x the origin's even for interactions that do almost nothing.
candidates.code_evidence: `<animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" from="0 0" to="0 -900" dur="40s" repeatCount="indefinite" />` (and 3 more at 28s, 18s and 50s); `transform: rotate(-28deg) rotateY(-6deg)`; `mask-image: var(--pricing-bg-fade)`; under `@media (max-width: 768px)` `.pricing-bg-svg { width: 220%; height: 110%; }`. History on main: added 7f0cac6b8 (Mar 24, live at the mid-May launch); mask and paths extended to -900..2700 in 8eb91ad64 (May 19); mobile box enlarged in 3e665743c (Jun 9).
candidates.measured_evidence: Desktop-1x with GPU on: a no-op background click is 40ms (2 delay / 0 processing / 38 presentation). With all animations stopped it is under 16; median across labels 48→24. With CSS animations off but SMIL still running, the 40-48ms floor stays, so SMIL is the desktop floor. Mobile-4x with all animations stopped (SMIL plus CSS): median 104→64, p75 136→88, INP-est 200→160, tap input delay 30-77 → 6-19ms, FAQ tab 88→32, burger 88→32. Idle with CSS animations off and SMIL running: 60 frames/s continues, mobile-4x renderer 170 ms/s, GPU main 479 ms/s. The production prefers-reduced-motion path gives the same mobile median of 64. Caveat: CDP CPU throttling does not slow the GPU or raster threads, so on real phones with weak GPUs at DPR 2.6-3 this is probably underestimated.
candidates.proposed_fix: Keep the same motion but move it to the compositor. Put each wave path in its own absolutely positioned `<svg>` (or div) inside the existing rotated, masked container. Replace each animateTransform with a CSS `@keyframes` translateY on that element, using the same distance (900 user units converted to %) and the same durations (40/28/18/50s, linear, infinite), with `will-change: transform`. Leave the 3D transform, the mask and the prefers-reduced-motion rule on the container unchanged. Each layer is rastered once and then only composited. Check with an idle trace: renderer frames should drop to about 0 and GPU-main busy should drop. Lower-effort fallback, with a visual change: `svg.pauseAnimations()` after a few seconds, or on pointerdown/keydown with resume on idle.
candidates.affects: Both: every interaction on the page, including no-op ones. Worst on phones (DPR, larger box since Jun 9, weak GPUs).
candidates.explains_timeline: Explains much of the May step and why it is pricing-specific: it went live with the new page in mid-May, and mask-image was added May 19. candidates.title: YourGPT chatbot (on every visit May 13 – Oct 6): leaked MutationObservers and URL-change re-renders on pricing's replaceState toggles
